why:
phase-483 W1 — the `Result`-returning session open that was `nros::init(locator, domain_id [, session_name [, node_namespace]])`. It moved into `rclcpp::` with the rest of the C++ API and took the `_in` suffix under RFC-0089's `_in` rule: upstream's `rclcpp::init` returns `void` and takes `(argc, argv)`, and `rclcpp::init(0, nullptr)` would otherwise bind ours through the null-pointer conversion, so an ours-only contract (an explicit locator and domain, a `Result` channel) needs a different NAME rather than a different signature. `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` and `rclcpp::init()` are upstream's and forward to it.

issue 1917 follow-up (2026-10-16) -- gains `init_in(int argc, char const* const* argv, const char* session_name = nullptr)`: the `Result`-returning twin of `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)`, honouring `--ros-args` exactly as it does (validate before a session opens, install after, close again on a rule that does not fit) but RETURNING a refusal where upstream's `void` shape forces an abort. It is the body `init_with_launch_auto` had, under the name of the family it belongs to. No overload ambiguity with `init_in(locator, domain_id)`: `nullptr` does not convert to `uint8_t`, so `init_in(0, nullptr)` picks this one, and no in-tree call passes a literal `0` locator.
